accent: The received high is the vowel of ri. The Taittirīya direct rendering marks it on the same syllable. Common pitch need not adjudicate the further historical stem analysis.
The healing-hymn readout follows the prior nominal; it lacks the independent high observed in the AV relative clause. The padapāṭha in TS keeps the low signs.

The received accented Śaunaka rendering has high on the first vowel. Its address is a yá-relative clause. The relative clause's retention condition under 8.1.66 is distinct from any general loṭ accent claim.
syntax: The first plural predicate stha takes the addressed herbs as subject and niṣkṛtīḥ/saṅkṛtīḥ as plural complement on their separate source addresses.
The next plural predicate sthana takes the same discourse addressees and patatriṇīḥ as a feminine plural predicate, alongside sīrāḥ or sarāḥ.
Mahīdhara supplies a possessive explanation in terms of spreading/movement. Sāyaṇa in Taittirīya gives the distinct leaf and return explanation.
In AVŚ 1.31.2 the yá-relative clause characterizes the guardians. The main release request is separately expressed by muñcata.
Kṣemakaraṇa Dāsa identifies the smaller clause's sthana with the same root as 02.0060 and loṭ. The relative reading remains explicit in the received-word interpretation.
contact: The s of jas gives ru and the selected visarga outcome before the sibilant of the separately owned as root under 8.3.36 with 8.3.15.
The Śākala pada retains niḥ separately. The joined sibilant in the corresponding part is prefix-derived ṣ under 8.3.41; the tense history of kṛtha stays Open.

observations: Mahīdhara quotes 6.1.106 exactly for patatriṇīḥ and paraphrases the plural as patatriṇyaḥ. His earlier short-i niṣkṛtīḥ has a separate paraphrase.
Mahīdhara gives tha→thana after the feminine plural and interprets the verb through bhavatha.
The received Śākala text has sthana. The cited Sāyaṇa line prints tana as the alternative ending label.
The direct segmented present pair preserves stha and sthana. Its plural is sam-kṛtīḥ with long ī in the named padapāṭha.
The Taittirīya Sāyaṇa gloss relates the term to a leaf and return; Mahīdhara relates it to motion or spread.
Śaunaka's relative clause prints sthána. The main verb separately requests release.
Whitney reports the commentary's unaspirated stana, distinct from the presence of aspiration in the received saṃhitā and pada.
The printed note explicitly assigns the form as-P2pl loṭ and 7.1.45 thana.
decisions: Accept the named long-ī plural under 6.1.106. The readout on the directly witnessed ṅīP form is independent of the short-i issue at the preceding noun.
Accept Mahīdhara's source-specific tha→thana construction. The transmitted tana label in the Ṛgvedic gloss stays explicit and does not silently revise the attested word.
Accept the independently named loṭ-ta analysis. It shares the word but preserves a different underlying affix and finite request.
Keep the direct aspirated word and the reported unaspirated commentary reading. Exact original commentary and the source’s use of tana or thana remain Open for stana.
Accept the case evidence for the received n-retaining and sam plural displays. Attribution of the short-i inflection to a specific Pāṇinian route is Open.
Keep the verb pair and the two nominal complements tied to the herb clause. The last distinct Śākala kṛtha and TS kṛta receive no word credit from their boundary attestation.
